The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
A day after President Trump said Russia would sell diesel to the U.S. and he says lower
prices in America, he's criticizing Ukrainian President Zelensky over the high fuel prices
as Ukraine continues to attack Russian refineries.
Speaking to reporters at the White House today, Trump said he would suggest Ukraine get a

Zelensky is furious about the deal, saying it would prolong the war Russia started.
And Piers Charles Mains has more on Zelensky's stance.
He said that the White House's decision prolongs the war by replenishing Russia's war chest.
Zelensky says the deal means more money for this war and more money to inflict suffering

And left unsaid, this deal gives Trump even more incentive to pressure Kiev to halt its

you know, on homes, on heating, electrical power stations, as we enter into the winter

NPR's Charles Mains reporting.
A weakening hurricane ECE is now a post-tropical storm, and it's being blamed for at least
four deaths.
As NPR's Bill Chappell reports, the storm ran through Alabama after making landfall on
the Florida coast last night.
One person died when a tree fell on a home in Escambia County, Florida.
That's just west of where ECE has made landfall as a Category 2 storm in the western Florida
panhandle.
Another person died in Birmingham, Alabama.
Here's Jefferson County Emergency Management Agency director Jim Coker.
We did have a storm-related fatality overnight, a tree did fall on the house.
ECE has weakened into a post-tropical cyclone on Saturday, but its heavy rains could continue
to cause flash flooding.
It's also bringing strong thunderstorms and potentially tornadoes to areas far from the
Gulf Coast.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
A growing number of voters are using AI chatbots to research their ballot and help decide between
candidates for the upcoming midterm elections.
NPR's Maham Javed reports the trend cuts across party lines.
One in five U.S. voters say they consult AI chatbots for election news and voting, and
the American Association of Political Consultants Foundation says Democratic and Republican
voters are using AI chatbots at similar rates.
There are concerns that the bots can be subtly persuasive and perhaps agreeable to a fault.
Adam Johnson is a voter in West Virginia who has used chatGPT to research his ballot.
ChatGPT is just kind of a people pleaser.
It just aims to please so whatever you lean towards it will speak positively about it.
Experts say these attributes can leave readers feeling more confident about their knowledge
without necessarily gaining more knowledge.
Maham Javed, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
At least nine people are dead in a shooting at a house in Erie, Pennsylvania overnight.
Police say the shooter is among the dead and there's no threat to the community.
Governor Josh Shapiro posted on social media that his heart breaks and says he's praying
for the community.
No word on the cause of the shooting and investigation is underway.
A report from the World Wildlife Fund chronicles a 73 percent drop in the average size of monitored
wildlife populations from 1970 until 2022.
NPR's Ari Daniel says that's according to the fund's biannual Living Planet report.
This year's index adds almost 300 species and the overall global decline in biodiversity
doesn't appear to be slowing down.
But the report points to a handful of species that have recovered or ticked upwards due
to sustained conservation efforts, bluefin tuna, green sea turtles, tigers, and certain
populations of elephants.
Rebecca Shaw is WWF's chief scientist.
This gives us hints into how we should be doing conservation overall to reduce the systems
that drive the degradation of nature.
The report says, quote, collective hope is the most reliable predictor we have of whether
large scale change will occur.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Consumers kept spending last month, according to the Bank of America Institute, and spending
data with lower income households spending the most.
The bank says spending was up 6.2 percent in September year over year.
Spending growth by lower income households has outpaced all but the highest earners.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
